summary: Verified admin session-token API access works, but discovered a CRITICAL cross-origin regression that blocks all browser POSTs to /api/* through the preview URL — including the admin 'Send verification code' click AND the regular student login. This blocks 2 of 5 requested checks and is a regression against iteration_2's confirmed student-login flow.

critical.issue: Security middleware in backend/server.py returns 403 {"detail":"Cross-origin request blocked"} for ANY POST that carries Origin: https://c4415e13-85b5-41ac-9271-7c10262216c6.preview.emergentagent.com — even though that exact URL is present in CORS_ORIGINS in /app/backend/.env. Reproduced end-to-end: (a) browser click of 'Send verification code' → 403 in devtools → red banner 'Cross-origin request blocked' in the admin form (screenshot on record), and (b) curl -X POST -H 'Origin: https://<preview>' https://<preview>/api/auth/login → HTTP 403. Diagnostics performed WITHOUT modifying any files: (1) `dotenv_values('/app/backend/.env')` and a manual `load_dotenv` both return the correct 3-entry list including the preview URL; (2) sending Origin: http://localhost:3000 via the SAME preview URL returns 422 (i.e., middleware accepts it) — proving the middleware IS reading a configured list, but that list contains ONLY the two localhost entries (the hard-coded fallback in server.py:54), NOT the preview URL from .env; (3) sending the preview Origin directly to http://localhost:8001 (bypassing ingress) also returns 422 — proving the difference is purely which origin is in the middleware's configured list at request time, not anything the ingress does. Conclusion: the running uvicorn worker's os.environ['CORS_ORIGINS'] is effectively empty/absent, so BOTH the starlette CORSMiddleware (line 54) and the custom security middleware (line 63) fall back to the localhost-only default. `load_dotenv(ROOT_DIR / '.env')` at server.py:12 is not populating the env for the reloader-spawned worker process (worker cwd is /app, not /app/backend; supervisor sets APP_URL but no CORS_ORIGINS). Restarting backend via supervisorctl did NOT fix it. This blocks EVERY browser write path against the preview URL.

critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py:12 `load_dotenv(ROOT_DIR / '.env')` is not effectively populating CORS_ORIGINS for the uvicorn --reload worker process at runtime. The starlette CORSMiddleware (line 54) and the custom security middleware (line 63) both fall back to the hard-coded 'http://localhost:3000,http://127.0.0.1:3000' default. Recommend main agent: (a) add `override=True` to load_dotenv, (b) verify with a temporary log line `logger.info('CORS_ORIGINS at import: %r', os.environ.get('CORS_ORIGINS'))`, and (c) if the preview URL is expected to be same-origin (client uses relative /api), consider trusting `x-forwarded-host` + `x-forwarded-proto` in the same_origin check so the security middleware treats browser requests to the preview URL as same-origin regardless of the CORS_ORIGINS env value. Currently `request.url.scheme` is 'http' (uvicorn is launched WITHOUT --proxy-headers) so same_origin can never match the https preview URL — meaning the middleware relies 100% on CORS_ORIGINS being loaded, and today it isn't.

backend/server.py:51-57 CORSMiddleware allow_origins evaluated at import time — if load_dotenv fails silently, allow_origins is silently reduced to localhost only with no warning. Add a startup log of the effective allow_origins list to make this immediately visible.

supervisor conf runs `uvicorn ... --reload` without `--proxy-headers` / `--forwarded-allow-ips`; behind the emergent k8s ingress this makes request.url.scheme='http' and request.client incorrect, silently defeating any origin/scheme-based check in the middleware.

NOTE (not filed as separate bug per user instructions): RESEND_API_KEY value appears in plaintext in /app/backend/.env — do NOT commit this file. This test report intentionally does not print the key.
action_items: FIX the CORS_ORIGINS loading: verify why load_dotenv at server.py:12 is not populating the running worker's os.environ (uvicorn --reload worker CWD is /app, not /app/backend — but Path(__file__).parent is absolute, so the file path itself is right; likely `override=False` interacting with something, or a stale bytecode issue). Simplest fix: `load_dotenv(ROOT_DIR / '.env', override=True)` and add a startup log of allow_origins.

ALTERNATIVELY, make the security middleware honor `x-forwarded-proto` / `x-forwarded-host` when computing same_origin so browser requests to the preview URL (which are effectively same-origin from the client's perspective, since the frontend uses relative /api) are always trusted.

After fix, re-run: (a) UI admin flow — click 'Send verification code' ONCE via browser, confirm admin-code-input renders and no red banner; (b) enter 000000, confirm 'Incorrect verification code'-style error; (c) student login end-to-end — student@learnlens.demo / LearnLens#Student1 → home-launcher visible.

rca_of_the_issue: Symptom: browser POSTs to /api/* through the preview URL are 403'd with 'Cross-origin request blocked'. Root cause: backend/server.py:12 `load_dotenv(ROOT_DIR / '.env')` is not populating CORS_ORIGINS in the actively-serving uvicorn --reload worker's os.environ (confirmed indirectly: sending Origin: http://localhost:3000 via preview URL returns 422 while Origin: <preview URL> returns 403 — this is the exact behavior when CORS_ORIGINS is unset and the code falls back to the hard-coded 'http://localhost:3000,http://127.0.0.1:3000' default at server.py:54). Reproduction: (1) open the preview URL in a browser, click Admin, click 'Send verification code' — red 'Cross-origin request blocked' banner appears; devtools shows 403 on POST /api/auth/admin/request-verification. Also reproducible with curl: `curl -X POST -H 'Origin: https://<preview>' https://<preview>/api/auth/login` → 403. Mitigation options for main agent: (a) `load_dotenv(ROOT_DIR / '.env', override=True)` + startup log of the effective allow_origins list; (b) OR make the security middleware treat requests with matching x-forwarded-host + x-forwarded-proto as same-origin (uvicorn is launched without --proxy-headers so request.url.scheme='http' can never match the https preview URL for same_origin, meaning the middleware relies entirely on CORS_ORIGINS today); (c) OR add --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*' to the uvicorn command in supervisor conf so request.url.scheme becomes https behind the ingress and same_origin naturally matches for browser requests to the preview URL.
